transcript.en: Good morning everyone. So today we're going to look at an important creative activity, and that's hand knitting.
transcript.zh: 大家早上好今天我们要来了解一项重要的创造性活动，手工编织。

transcript.en: Ancient knitted garments have been found in many different countries, showing that knitting is a global activity with a long history.
transcript.zh: 在许多不同的国家都发现了古代针织服装，这表明编织是一项历史悠久的全球性活动。

transcript.en: When someone says the word 'knitting' we might well picture an elderly person-
transcript.zh: 当有人说“编织”这个词时，我们很可能会想到一位老人——

transcript.en: a grandmother perhaps-sitting by the fire knitting garments for themselves or other members of the family.
transcript.zh: 也许是一位奶奶——坐在火边为自己或其他家庭成员编织衣服。

transcript.en: It's a homely image, but one that may lead you to feel that knitting is an activity of the past-
transcript.zh: 这是一个家常的画面，但可能会让你觉得编织是一种老旧的活动。

transcript.en: and,indeed, during the previous decade, it was one of the skills that was predicted to vanish from everyday life.
transcript.zh: 确实，在过去的十年里，它是一种预计会从日常生活中消失的技能。

transcript.en: For although humans have sewn and knitted their own clothing for a very long time.
transcript.zh: 因为尽管人类缝纫和编织自己的衣服已经有很长一段时间了，

transcript.en: many of these craft-based skills went into decline when industrial machines took over-
transcript.zh: 但当工业机器接管时，许多这些基于手工艺的技能开始衰落。

transcript.en: mainly because they were no longer passed down from one generation to another.
transcript.zh: 主要是因为这些手工艺不再代代相传。

transcript.en: However, that's all changing and interest in knitting classes in many countries is actually rising,as more and more people are seeking formal instruction in the skill.
transcript.zh: 然而，这一切都在发生变化，许多国家对编织课程的兴趣实际上正在上升，因为越来越多的人正在寻求该技能的正规指导。

transcript.en: With that trend, we're also seeing an increase in the sales figures for knitting equipment.
transcript.zh: 随着这一趋势，我们也看到编织设备的销售量有所增加。

transcript.en: So why do people want to be taught to knit at a time when a machine can readily do the job for them?
transcript.zh: 那么，为什么人们想要在机器可以轻松为他们完成工作的时候学习编织呢？

transcript.en: The answer is that knitting, as a handicraft, has numerous benefits for those doing it.
transcript.zh: 答案是，编织作为一种手工艺品，对做这件事的人有很多好处。

transcript.en: Let's consider what some of these might be.
transcript.zh: 让我们来想想有哪些好处。

transcript.en: While many people knitted garments in the past because they couldn't afford to buy clothes,
transcript.zh: 虽然过去许多人因为买不起衣服而编织服装，

transcript.en: it's still true today that knitting can be helpful if you're experiencing economic hardship.
transcript.zh: 但现在仍然如此，如果您遇到经济困难，编织会有所帮助。

transcript.en: If you have several children who all need warm winter clothes, knitting may save you a lot of money.
transcript.zh: 如果你有几个孩子都需要暖和的冬衣，编织可以为你节省很多钱。

transcript.en: And the results of knitting your own clothes can be very rewarding,
transcript.zh: 自己编织衣服是有价值的，

transcript.en: even though the skills you need to get going are really quite basic, and the financial outlay is minimal.
transcript.zh: 即便你开始工作所需的技能确实非常基本并且财务支出很少。

transcript.en: But the more significant benefits in today’s world are to do with well-being.
transcript.zh: 然而它在当今世界更重要的好处是它与幸福感有关。

transcript.en: In a world where it's estimated that we spend up to nine hours a day online,doing something with our hands that is craft based, makes us feel good.
transcript.zh: 在一个我们每天预计在线工作长达 9 小时的世界里，用我们的双手做一些手工制作的事情会让我们感到美好。

transcript.en: It releases us from the stress of a technological, fast-paced life.
transcript.zh: 它使我们摆脱了科技、快节奏生活的压力。

transcript.en: Now let's look back a bit to early knitting activities.
transcript.zh: 现在，让我们回顾一下早期的编织活动。

transcript.en: In fact, no one really knows when knitting first began,but archaeological remains have disclosed plenty of information for us to think about.
transcript.zh: 事实上，没有人真正知道编织最初是从什么时候开始的，但考古遗迹揭示了大量信息供我们参考。

transcript.en: One of the interesting things about knitting. Is that the earliest pieces of clothing that have been found suggest that most of the items produced were round rather than flat.
transcript.zh: 关于针织的有趣之处之一是，在发现的最早的衣服中，生产的大部分衣物都是圆形的而不是扁平的。

transcript.en: Discoveries from the 3rd and 4th centuries in Egypt show that things like socks and gloves,
transcript.zh: 埃及 3 世纪和 4 世纪的发现表明，袜子和手套等

transcript.en: that were needed to keep hands and feet warm,were knitted in one piece, using four or five needles.
transcript.zh: 给手脚保暖的东西是用四到五根针编织成一件的。

transcript.en: That's very different from most knitting patterns today, which only require two.
transcript.zh: 这与当今大多数针织图案大不相同，后者只需要两个。

transcript.en: What's more, the very first needles people used were hand carved out of wood and other natural materials,like bone,
transcript.zh: 更重要的是，人们使用的第一根针是用木头和其他天然材料（如骨头）手工雕刻而成，

transcript.en: whereas today's needles are largely made of steel or plastic and make that characteristic clicking sound when someone's using them.
transcript.zh: 而今天的针主要由钢或塑料制成，当有人使用它们时会发出特有的咔嗒声。

transcript.en: Ancient people knitted using yarns made from linen, hemp, cotton and wool, and these were often very rough on the skin.
transcript.zh: 古代人使用由亚麻、大麻、棉花和羊毛制成的纱线进行编织，这些纱线在皮肤上通常非常粗糙。

transcript.en: The spinning wheel, which allowed people to make finer yarns and produce much greater quantities of them,
transcript.zh: 纺纱轮使人们能够制造更细的纱线并生产更多的纱线，

transcript.en: led to the dominance of wool in the knitting industry - often favoured for its warmth.
transcript.zh: 致使因其保暖性而受到青睐的羊毛在针织行业占据主导地位。

transcript.en: Another interesting fact about knitting is that because it was practised in so many parts of the world for so many purposes,regional differences in style developed.
transcript.zh: 关于针织的另一个有趣的事实是，因为它在世界上如此多的地方被用于不同的目的，因此风格上的区域差异得以发展。

transcript.en: This visual identity has allowed researchers to match bits of knitted clothing that have been unearthed over time to the region
transcript.zh: 这种视觉识别使研究人员能够将不同时间出土的针织服装碎片

transcript.en: from which the wearer came or the job that he or she did. As I've mentioned, knitting offered people from poor communities a way of making extra money while doing other tasks.
transcript.zh: 与穿衣者来自的地区或他所做的工作相匹配。正如我所提到的，编织为贫困社区的人们提供了一种在做其他工作的同时赚取额外收入的方式。

transcript.en: For many centuries, it seems, men, women and children took every opportunity to knit, for example, while watching over sheep, walking to market or riding in boats.
transcript.zh: 许多世纪以来，男人、女人和儿童似乎都在利用一切机会编织，例如，在看羊、步行去市场或乘船时。

transcript.en: So let's move on to take a...
transcript.zh: 所以，让我们继续采取...
